subject.title: Feature: config option to route gateway lifecycle warnings to a dedicated channel

question: Should OpenClaw add a general internal-warning destination/category router under messages, and what categories/defaults should it support relative to existing suppression and cron failure destinations?
rationale: Source inspection proves the routing gap, but the permanent public config contract and warning-delivery precedence cross core message delivery, cron, and channel behavior and need maintainer intent.

options.title: Approve default-compatible router
options.body: Add an explicit opt-in router for lifecycle, tool-error, and system-notice warnings while preserving active-channel delivery by default.

options.title: Keep suppression-only policy
options.body: Treat messages.suppressToolErrors and cron.failureDestination as the supported operator controls and narrow this request to docs or channel-specific leaks.

options.title: Split by warning class
options.body: Handle lifecycle warnings, transient tool errors, and cron notifications as separate narrower issues instead of a general router.

recommendation.title: Approve default-compatible router
recommendation.body: Add an explicit opt-in router for lifecycle, tool-error, and system-notice warnings while preserving active-channel delivery by default.

likelyOwner.reason: They have recent adjacent warning-delivery history and are the strongest routing candidate among the inspected current-main provenance.
